cards.text: This is the LORD's word through the prophet Zechariah (Zechariah 1:1), and it's about Jerusalem. The LORD says, "Behold, a day of the LORD is coming when your plunder will be divided in your presence." Then He says He will gather all the nations for battle against Jerusalem.

cards.question: All the nations come for battle against Jerusalem. What happens to the city?

cards.text: The houses are looted, and the women ravished. Then the LORD tells what happens to the people of the city.

cards.question: When Jerusalem is captured, every last person in the city is carried off into exile.

cards.text: Half the city goes into exile, but the rest of the people stay in the city. And then somebody goes out to fight against those nations.

cards.question: Who goes out to fight against the nations that came against Jerusalem?

cards.text: And here's where it gets BIG, friend. On that day His feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem.

cards.question: When the LORD's feet stand on the Mount of Olives, what happens to the mountain?

cards.text: It splits from east to west into a great valley, half the mountain moving north and half moving south. Friend, I can't break ONE cookie in half without crumbs going everywhere, and the LORD splits a MOUNTAIN.

cards.question: Jerusalem is under attack, and a brand new valley just opened up. The LORD says, "You will ___ by My mountain valley."

cards.text: The valley reaches all the way to Azal, and you'll flee the way you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah, king of Judah. Then the prophet says the LORD his God will come, and He's not coming alone.

cards.question: The prophet says the LORD his God will come. Who comes with Him?

cards.text: On that day there will be no light, no cold or frost, a unique day known only to the LORD, without day or night. Don't look at me for the date, friend: I spent YEARS in a junk drawer not even knowing what day it WAS.

cards.question: On that unique day, when evening comes, it gets dark like any other evening.

cards.text: And on that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem. This chapter just keeps going, friend.

cards.question: Where does the living water flowing out from Jerusalem go?

answers.text: Half toward each sea east and west
All of it toward the Eastern Sea
All of it toward the Western Sea

cards.question: The living water from Jerusalem flows in summer and winter alike.

cards.text: Now here comes the line I'd frame and hang over every oven in my bakery. It's about who rules over all the earth.

cards.question: On that day the LORD will become ___ over all the earth.

cards.text: "The LORD alone, and His name alone." King over ALL the earth, and me? I'm in charge of one little cookie planet, and my oven STILL doesn't listen to me.

All the land from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem, turns into a plain, but Jerusalem is raised up and stays in her place, from gate to gate and tower to winepresses. Everything around it goes flat and Jerusalem RISES, like the one cookie in my batch that actually puffs up right.

cards.question: Even after being raised up, Jerusalem will face utter destruction again someday.

cards.text: People will live there, and Jerusalem will dwell securely. Then the LORD turns to the peoples who warred against Jerusalem, and He strikes them with a plague.

cards.question: What does the LORD's plague do to the peoples who warred against Jerusalem?

answers.text: Their flesh rots as they stand
Their cities fall into the sea

cards.text: On that day a great panic from the LORD comes upon them.

cards.question: When a great panic from the LORD comes on the peoples who warred against Jerusalem, what do they do?

cards.text: Judah will also fight at Jerusalem. Now remember how this chapter started, with Jerusalem's plunder divided right in front of them?

cards.question: This time it's the wealth of all the surrounding nations. What happens to it?

answers.text: It is collected in great abundance
It is scattered across the land
It is all sent back home

cards.text: A similar plague strikes the horses, mules, camels and donkeys in those camps. Then comes a turn I did NOT see coming, and it's about the survivors from those same nations.

cards.question: What will the survivors from the nations that came against Jerusalem do year after year?

answers.text: Go up to worship the King

cards.question: Year after year, the survivors go up to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts. Which feast do they come to celebrate?

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks about any families of the earth that don't go up to Jerusalem to worship the King.

cards.question: If any families of the earth don't go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, then the ___ will not fall on them.

cards.text: Then the LORD names one nation in particular: Egypt.

cards.question: If the people of Egypt don't go up to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles, the rain will still fall on them.

cards.text: This will be the punishment of Egypt and of all the nations that don't go up. Then, on that day, words get inscribed on the bells of the horses.

cards.question: On that day, ___ TO THE LORD will be inscribed on the bells of the horses.

cards.text: The cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the sprinkling bowls before the altar, and every pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts. EVERY POT, friend, and I thought going from a 25-cent bin to a gold base was a big glow-up.

cards.question: On that day, there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Hosts.
